## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
Deleting `app/defaults.json` must be fixed before merge, because `load_defaults()` in `app/startup.py` still reads that file and will raise on every call. `is_valid_port` also rejects port 65535, and `load_config` hides every failure behind `{}`.

## Changes
This pull request adds millisecond parsing to `parse_timeout`, and adds the new helpers `is_valid_port`, `load_config` (with an optional `ujson` accelerator) and `normalize_host`, with tests for each. It also deletes `app/defaults.json` and adds a reviewer doc and a test fixture.

## Critical
- app/defaults.json:1 [base] — correctness — Restore defaults.json or update load_defaults — Every call to `load_defaults()` now raises `FileNotFoundError`, because the file is deleted. `app/startup.py:6` still runs `Path(__file__).with_name("defaults.json").read_text()`, and nothing in the diff changes that caller. — Any startup path that loads application defaults crashes once this merges. — Fix: Keep `app/defaults.json`, or change `app/startup.py:6` to use the new source of defaults in the same pull request.

## Important
- app/parse.py:22 — correctness — Accept port 65535 in is_valid_port — `is_valid_port(65535)` returns `False`, because `0 < p < 65535` excludes the upper bound. The docstring promises "1-65535". `tests/test_parse.py:16` checks only the lower bound, so nothing catches this. — Configs or callers that use port 65535 are rejected as invalid. — Fix: `0 < p <= 65535`, and add an upper-bound case next to `test_is_valid_port_lower_bound`.
- app/parse.py:30 — silent-failure — Stop returning {} for every load_config error — A missing file, a permission error or malformed JSON all return `{}`, because `except Exception` swallows them with no log or signal to the caller. No comment explains the fallback; the docstring says only "Load the JSON config at path". — A typo in a config file silently runs the app with empty config, and operators get no indication of why their settings were ignored. — Fix: Catch only `FileNotFoundError` if a missing file should mean empty config, and let decode and permission errors propagate or log them.

## Suggestions
- app/parse.py:35 — comments — Fix normalize_host docstring for empty input — The docstring says "returns None when h is empty", but `normalize_host("")` returns `""` (line 37: `return ""`). — Callers that follow the docstring and check `is None` will treat an empty host as valid. — Fix: Decide which return value is intended, then update either the docstring or line 37 so they match.
- app/parse.py:40 — tests — Cover the trailing-dot and empty branches of normalize_host — `normalize_host("Example.COM.")` and `normalize_host("")` are never exercised. `test_normalize_host_lowercases` passes input with no trailing dot, so the strip on lines 40-41 and the early return on line 36 are untested. — A regression in stripping fully qualified names or in empty-input handling would not fail any test. — Fix: Extend `test_normalize_host_lowercases` with trailing-dot and empty-string cases.
